title: Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: The exhaust fan motor is not running at expected speed.
fullDescription:
E1 on an LG range hood indicates the main exhaust fan motor is not reaching its commanded speed. The control board monitors the motor tachometer and triggers E1 when feedback is absent or out of range.

Root causes include a failed motor, obstruction in the blower housing (e.g., grease buildup), or a wiring fault. Heavy grease on the squirrel cage is a common culprit after years without cleaning.

Service starts with a deep cleaning of the blower assembly before replacing hardware.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off power at the breaker.

fixSteps.title: Remove filters
fixSteps.instruction: Take out baffle or mesh filters.

fixSteps.title: Clean blower
fixSteps.instruction: Degrease the blower wheel and housing.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If motor fails to start, install a new blower motor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the hood is installed above an island or at a height requiring lifting help.
videoSearchQuery: LG range hood E1 error fix

faq.q: How often should I clean the blower?
faq.a: Every 3-6 months depending on cooking frequency.

faq.q: Can I run the hood with E1?
faq.a: No airflow will occur; clean or service first.

title: Speed Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The motor speed feedback sensor is reporting invalid data.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates the hood's speed sensor (hall-effect or tachometer) on the fan motor is providing invalid or no feedback to the control board. The hood cannot regulate speed accurately and disables the fan.

The sensor is typically integrated with the motor or mounted on the control PCB. Failures are often the result of heat or grease ingress.

On most LG models, the sensor is not serviceable separately, so a blower motor replacement is required.

fixSteps.title: Access motor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove grease filters and upper housing to access the motor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the sensor harness and look for grease contamination.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the motor and harness check good.
videoSearchQuery: LG range hood E2 error fix

faq.a: Rarely — it's usually part of the motor assembly.
Sometimes if grease caused the connector to fail; worth trying first.

title: Lighting Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The cooktop lighting circuit is shorted or open.
fullDescription:
E3 indicates a fault in the hood's lighting circuit. LED modules or halogen lamps may have failed, or the lighting driver board has shorted.

Replace burned-out bulbs first, then inspect the LED driver if present. On LED hoods, a failed driver typically takes out multiple LEDs at once and must be replaced as an assembly.

Lighting faults don't affect ventilation but will persistently display E3 until cleared.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off breaker and let lamps cool.

fixSteps.title: Inspect bulbs
fixSteps.instruction: Remove bulb covers and test each lamp/LED.

fixSteps.title: Replace driver
fixSteps.instruction: If all LEDs are dead, replace the LED driver board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the driver replacement doesn't resolve E3.
videoSearchQuery: LG range hood E3 light error fix

faq.q: Can the hood still vent with E3?
faq.a: Yes, only the lighting is affected.

faq.q: What bulb type does my hood use?
faq.a: Check the label inside the hood; LG uses either LED modules or G4/G9 halogens depending on model.

title: Touch Panel Error
shortDescription: The touch control panel has detected a stuck button or moisture.
fullDescription:
E4 indicates the touch panel is registering a continuous input, either from a stuck sensor or moisture on the control surface. The hood locks the controls until the fault clears.

Wipe the panel dry and ensure no grease residue is present, as both can trigger phantom touches. A deep clean usually clears E4.

If the code returns, the touch PCB may need replacement.

fixSteps.title: Clean panel
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe thoroughly with degreaser and dry with microfiber.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If E4 persists, replace the touch control board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if cleaning and power cycling don't clear E4.
videoSearchQuery: LG range hood E4 error fix

A mild degreaser or diluted dish soap applied to a cloth, never directly on the panel.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Communication between control boards has been lost.
fullDescription:
E5 signals that the main PCB cannot communicate with the user interface board or a secondary module. Cable issues, a failing board, or power anomalies are the typical culprits.

Power cycle first, then reseat any ribbon or harness connectors reachable after removing the filter area cover. Many E5 events are cured by a firm connector reseat.

Persistent E5 after reseating usually means a board replacement is required.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Breaker off for 5 minutes and back on.

fixSteps.title: Access boards
fixSteps.instruction: Remove filters and any service panel to expose boards.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Firmly reseat each ribbon and harness connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If E5 persists, replace UI board first.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if reseating doesn't help and you're unsure which board to swap.
videoSearchQuery: LG range hood E5 error fix

faq.q: Does LG cover this under warranty?

title: Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The hood temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
E6 indicates the hood's temperature sensor — used to detect heat from the cooktop and trigger auto-boost mode — is open or shorted. The hood will revert to manual control when this fault is active.

The sensor is typically located near the hood's underside, facing down at the cooktop. It can be fouled by grease or damaged by excessive heat.

Cleaning the sensor may resolve false readings; if not, replacement is straightforward.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe sensor with a degreaser-dampened cloth.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance; compare to LG spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in new sensor and reseat connector.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you cannot access the sensor or if E6 returns after replacement.
videoSearchQuery: LG range hood E6 sensor fix

faq.q: Does E6 stop the hood from working?
faq.a: No, only auto mode is lost; manual control still works.

faq.q: How often should the sensor be cleaned?

title: Filter Maintenance Reminder
shortDescription: The hood is reminding you to clean or replace filters.
fullDescription:
E7 is a maintenance reminder, not a hardware fault. It indicates the hood has logged sufficient hours of use to require filter cleaning or replacement.

Mesh grease filters should be washed in the dishwasher or by hand with degreaser. Charcoal filters (in ductless installations) need periodic replacement — typically every 6 months.

After service, press and hold the Reset button (often the Filter or Timer button) for 3-5 seconds to clear E7.

causes.cause: Reset not performed after previous cleaning

fixSteps.title: Remove filters
fixSteps.instruction: Slide out mesh or baffle filters.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Wash mesh filters with degreaser or replace charcoal filters.

fixSteps.title: Reset indicator
fixSteps.instruction: Press and hold Filter/Reset button for 3-5 seconds.

whenToCallPro: Not usually needed — this is user-serviceable.

title: Main Board Fault
shortDescription: The main control board has reported an internal fault.
fullDescription:
E8 indicates the main control PCB has detected an internal fault, such as a failed relay, corrupted memory, or power supply anomaly. The hood typically disables all functions until serviced.

Power cycling may clear transient events, but repeated E8 errors require board replacement. In some cases a firmware update via LG service can resolve the issue.

This is generally not a DIY-friendly repair unless you are comfortable with electronics work.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Remove filters and check for any visible damage on the main board.

fixSteps.title: Contact LG
fixSteps.instruction: Request warranty service or firmware check.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro — main board work involves line voltage and careful handling.
videoSearchQuery: LG range hood E8 error fix

faq.a: Usually within the first year; check your documentation.

faq.q: Can a surge protector prevent E8?
faq.a: It can reduce the risk of surge-related board failures.
